name: Florida Science Standards Review Work Timeline
about: Dated public milestones in the independent review of Florida's proposed 2026 science standards.

item.name: Review work began; research snapshot and public-record check
item.description: The project author confirms that review work began on October 22, 2026. The primary comparison and corpus/process reports identify that date as the first research cutoff, document checks of the FDOE review portal, and record that preserved 2026 draft PDFs matched the portal copies by SHA-256 on the check date.

item.name: Review hub and comparative analyses published
item.description: Repository history records publication of the standards review hub, then revisions on predecessor standards, omissions, sectarian framing, provenance, authorship and AI disclosure, public summaries, learning order, and workload methods.

item.name: Interactive graph and source coverage added
item.description: Repository history records the first interactive benchmark/source graph, shareable graph items, and source coverage reporting. The viewer now supports selecting a node from search or the graph, refocusing its network, and choosing a recorded-connection depth.

item.name: Organization research site published
item.description: The Florida Citizens for Science organization site and standards-review section were published on GitHub Pages, with forwarding links from the earlier personal-site location.

item.name: Knowledge graph expanded and update rules consolidated
item.description: The graph was expanded with all 498 Florida 2008 benchmark IDs, 208 NGSS Performance Expectations, 412 Indiana K–8 statements, ten complete grade-level blocks from the 2007 Florida Citizens for Science proposal, and fifteen ancillary document records. It distinguishes 3,354 machine-ranked leads from reviewed assertions, updates corpus coverage notes, and links original FCAT workbooks. A shared update-rules guide was added to keep the timeline, corpus register, graph, reports, and disclosures synchronized.

item.name: Graph explorer improved for public and educator workflows
item.description: A multi-reviewer usability pass improved graph filtering, source discovery, keyboard access, evidence-aware relationship displays, and discovery of the current curriculum-material inventory. Search results can now open source records; source-only records are clearly identified; result selection and graph focus stay linked; and the viewer explains where literal and semantic search differ. The scope is recorded in commit 9d21d59.

item.name: Similarity leads and offline semantic search linked from the explorer
item.description: Selected graph items now show machine-ranked similarity candidates in a section distinct from reviewed relationships, with scores and an explicit unreviewed warning. Item wording can seed a local corpus semantic-search command. Focused graph layouts now expand ring spacing by layer size and hide labels only on crowded layers while retaining keyboard-operable nodes and accessible names. The author and acknowledgements page records AI-agent review and implementation assistance. Changes are recorded in commit fd18dc0.

item.name: Omission analysis adds instructional-integrity implications
item.description: The full report, plain-language brief, rhetoric audit, and omission crosswalk now explain how concentrated evolution and climate omissions may fragment explanatory learning and shift synthesis work to local teachers and materials. The analysis distinguishes these pedagogical risks from proof of classroom outcomes, acknowledges retained climate and evolution content, and cites the National Academies K–12 framework and the 2024 U.S. Climate Literacy Guide. Changes are recorded in commit 55c2479.

item.name: Placement crosswalk updated with omissions and teaching consequences
item.description: The evolution/climate placement page now identifies specific omitted evolution expectations and climate-attribution/forecasting tasks in its normalized takeaways, explains possible consequences for coherent and accurate teaching, and corrects stale 2026 register totals to the current 1,512-item inventory. Changes are recorded in commit 7a56ebb.

item.name: Political-history evidence and project bibliography published
item.description: The review foregrounds the history while naming the substantive omissions in the overview, comparison, subject analyses, plain-language brief, commentary, and shareable posts: no numbered evolution benchmark or common-ancestry synthesis; no equivalent human-evolution expectations; and no numbered climate-change benchmark or explicit climate-attribution/forecasting tasks. A project-wide bibliography includes publisher and DOI links, expandable source notes and BibTeX records, and a consolidated download. Local source copies and hashes are preserved in the research corpus. These records make the omissions politically salient but do not establish the 2026 workgroup's motive. Published in commit 91a7b7e; the GitHub Pages build succeeded.

item.name: Source graph guide and full-viewport app published
item.description: The source-graph guide now introduces the data and evidence limits before launching a dedicated full-viewport app. The app keeps its control sidebar, menu, and live status footer fixed while the SVG canvas pans and zooms inside the viewport. Source details open in a dialog; source-map layouts can be regrouped, and users can export SVG, PNG, filtered JSON, or the full graph. Published in commit ca760d5; the GitHub Pages build succeeded.

item.name: Benchmark map spacing and source locator links improved and published
item.description: The benchmark network now opens focused on the full 2026 draft and spaces nodes dynamically within grade/course bands, with a 400% zoom ceiling. Source-map lines distinguish recorded comparison assertions from additional source files explicitly named in composite-item locators. Locator-derived connections are labeled as source context, not benchmark-equivalence claims. Published in commit de83b9e; the GitHub Pages build succeeded.

item.name: Review landing page reorganized as a visual walkthrough
item.description: The review landing page was reorganized as a six-chapter visual walkthrough covering the draft, evolution and climate omissions, benchmark coverage, an explanatory topic map, Florida’s adoption history, and evidence limits. A chapter navigator marks the current section; detailed pages open in new tabs so readers can return to their place. Published in commit b6cf66b; the GitHub Pages build succeeded.

dateBasis: The project author confirms that work began on 2026-10-22. Subsequent research and publication milestones are based on report-stated cutoffs, explicit source-check dates, and dated repository commit history. The timeline does not capture every off-repository activity.
